prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
Factories around the world are making a big promise about AI. But many have not yet made it part of everyday production.

By September 2026, several independent signals show that investment plans are rising quickly. A robotics group says new industrial robot installations in 2024 were more than twice the level of ten years earlier. It also names AI and self-directed robots as the top robotics trend for 2026.

The money is moving before the full change can be seen on every factory floor.

One survey of 600 manufacturing leaders found that 80 percent expect to put at least 20 percent of their improvement budget into smart manufacturing tools. These include automation equipment, sensors, data systems, and AI that can take actions on its own.

But plans are not the same as working systems. Another industry survey found that only 9 percent of companies were already using robots and other machines with a high level of independence. The share expected to use them within two years rose to 22 percent.

That gap matters.

China has placed AI robotics at the center of its national industrial strategy. Its humanoid robots have appeared in high-profile public demonstrations. Yet one robotics group says that, in real production settings, their abilities are still mainly limited to demonstrations and pilot projects.

There is also a second story inside the AI investment story. Some factories are being asked to build the tools that AI needs. More than $500 billion has been announced for U.S. semiconductor manufacturing, or the making of computer chips. Demand is also rising for power equipment used by data centers. The Federal Reserve says several districts connected stronger factory activity with data-center orders.

So a rise in manufacturing activity can come from two different paths. AI may change how a factory works. Or factories may produce the chips, power systems, and equipment needed by the wider AI economy. The first path is still developing. The second is already creating visible demand.

【Point One】
The robot story is not moving at the same speed everywhere. In 2024, global installations reached 542,000, still 2 percent below an earlier peak. In the U.S., the preliminary 2025 total rose 11 percent to 38,000. Food installations rose sharply, while automotive installations fell slightly. New growth is spreading beyond the traditional automotive base.

【Point Two】
A stronger manufacturing report should be read carefully. More than $500 billion has been announced for chip manufacturing, while data-center demand is lifting orders for power equipment. Several Federal Reserve districts linked stronger factory activity with those orders. That shows AI-related demand, but not necessarily AI running the shop floor.
